On the other hand, fatigue failure (crack initiation) is caused by notch features within the structure where the loads shall be analyzed accurately. It can stated that the FLS is a very site-dependent assessment. The FLS results within this deliverable have been assessed under two different site E.C.s. - Site 1: MTV moored offshore in a site with waves and medium current velocity. The Florida ocean data has been considered as a representative case. Final Technical Report 26/57 - Site 2: MTV in jack-up configuration in a site with high current speed, and the effects of the waves can be considered negligible. Admiralty Inlet has been selected since there is a significant record of current data available. The results show a minimum lifetime of 9-12 years corresponding to the tube under the maximum CEC size under open site E.C (site 1), assuming a certain utilization factor. Under rivers/estuaries (site 2) with a maximum current of 4 m/s, this lifecycle is extended to well over 25 years. The final design of the supporting structure is depicted in the following figure. Figure 6-3 Supporting structure; stiffeners distribution Final Technical Report 27/57 7 MOORING SYSTEM DESIGN The intrinsic versatility of the MTV requires it to have multiple mooring systems suitable for different deployment sites, water depths, and environmental conditions. For shallow waters, an internal mooring system is proposed, while for deeper waters, the MTV would be attached to a preexisting mooring system. The MTV is equipped with 4 mooring points for the external mooring case, and it would allow for mooring the vessel in as many configurations as this allows, the most common configurations being a four-point mooring or a single-point mooring. For rivers and estuaries, a jack-up system is envisaged. Numerical simulations were carried out in the commercial software OrcaFlex by Orcina. The detailed design of the jack-up system was outsourced to experts in these types of systems by sharing with them information about working and environmental conditions and by providing them with the scantling of the legs based on a global analysis performed. 7.1 Internal Mooring System The internal mooring system is composed of 4 mooring lines, which will be normally deployed at the same time. In some locations where environmental loads do not reverse in direction, a 2 line configuration might also be possible. This mooring system will be equipped on board and will consist of chain sections and drag anchors, as can be seen in Figure 7-1. This system will be appropriate for mooring the vessel in sites with depths of up to 50 m using catenary mooring lines.
